title: Prove Feuerbach distance relations via coordinate computation

problemStatement.plain: The nine-point circle is tangent to the incircle and all three excircles. Core distance relations: |NI| = |R/2 - r| and |NI_a| = R/2 + r_a.

proven: All 9 points on nine-point circle (3 midpoints, 3 Euler midpoints, 3 altitude feet)

knowledge.progressSummary: PROGRESS: Proved 8 new general theorems: Heron formula (squared), dot product polarization, 3 circumcenter dot product identities, side length positivity (3), circumradius positivity, unsquared extended law of sines. Complete algebraic backbone for abstract Feuerbach proof chain.

insights: General Feuerbach distance proofs blocked by sqrt in side lengths: incenter coords involve a=sqrt(...), cross terms a*b resist ring tactic
NI = R/2 - r (Feuerbach incircle tangency) follows from Euler identity, but proving either requires eliminating sqrt
Excircle tangency d(N,I_k) = R/2 + r_k verified numerically for 3-4-5 triangle (all 3 cases)
The equilateral_R_eq_2r proof in main file was broken by Mathlib v4.26 upgrade (dist2_sq unfold change) - independently proved in OQ01
Approach for general case: introduce a^2, b^2, c^2 as polynomial constraints and use nlinarith - untested but promising
Extended law of sines (squared) IS provable as polynomial identity - key was rw [sq_abs] to eliminate |x|² before ring
General Feuerbach proof chain: ext_law_of_sines → sigma_identity → Euler OI²=R²-2Rr → NI=(R/2-r)
FUNDAMENTAL OBSTACLE: incenter coords involve side_a/side_b/side_c (sqrt). Products a·b resist ring. Need reformulation without sqrt or algebraic elimination.
Abstract inner-product proof of Feuerbach: N-I = [(s-a)(A-O)+(s-b)(B-O)+(s-c)(C-O)]/(2s), then |N-I|^2 expands via bilinearity using <X-O,Y-O>=R^2-|X-Y|^2/2
Key chain: bilinearity → |u|^2 = R^2*s^2 - sigma → sigma_identity → Heron → NI^2 = (R/2-r)^2
Polarization identity <P-R,Q-R> = (|R-P|^2+|R-Q|^2-|P-Q|^2)/2 is the bridge between dot products and distances
Heron formula (squared) is polynomial in coords: unfold side lengths, area, then ring
Unsquared ext law of sines follows from squared version via eq_of_sq_eq_nonneg (both sides positive)
nextSteps: Formalize the bilinear expansion of |u|^2 where u=(s-a)(A-O)+(s-b)(B-O)+(s-c)(C-O)
Show |u|^2 = R^2*s^2 - sigma using dot_circumcenter lemmas
Connect sigma_identity + Heron to get |u|^2 = R^2*s^2 - abcs + 4*Area^2
Derive NI^2 = (R/2-r)^2 using abc = 4R*Area and r = Area/s
Extend to excircle tangency: NI_k = R/2 + r_k
